frequency_question: How often does a congressional joint resolution of disapproval successfully pass both chambers to block a major executive foreign nuclear or arms agreement within the review window?
membership_rule: Includes all formal congressional reviews of Section 123 agreements or major Middle East arms sales where a joint resolution of disapproval was formally introduced and brought to a vote. Excludes informal consultations or resolutions that failed to pass committees.
coverage_note: 4 named major parliamentary showdowns; covers all substantive legislative veto attempts on Middle East nuclear/arms pacts since the Arms Export Control Act and AEA statutory frameworks matured.
known_gaps: Excludes minor non-controversial 123 agreements that tacitly passed without floor challenges.
skeleton: Four decades of legislative-executive nuclear and sensitive arms review battles, categorized by polarized versus bipartisan eras.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 4 major contested historical showdowns where disapproval resolutions reached floor votes.
validity_reason: Institutional dynamics between the executive and legislative branches regarding foreign pacts shift slowly over decades based on war powers and statutory frameworks.
